web_evidence.title: Excerpt from Buckeye by Patrick Ryan
web_evidence.note: The four-page excerpt, reproduced with Random House permission, sustains third-person narration around Cal and Margaret and moves into characters’ perceptions without a participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: Patrick Ryan on the Secrets of the Omniscient Narrator
web_evidence.note: Ryan explicitly describes Buckeye as a third-person, multiple-perspective, omniscient-leaning novel and says he established that narrator’s mobility as a contract to honor throughout the book.

web_evidence.title: 4 lives are upended by an impulsive kiss in the epic novel 'Buckeye'
web_evidence.note: Maureen Corrigan’s NPR review explicitly identifies an omniscient narrator who moves among the four main characters’ points of view and describes the novel’s chapter-level range.

person_note: The controlling voice is a nonparticipating third-person omniscient narrator that moves among multiple characters and generations. Numerous interior Goodreads passages independently show third-person access to Felix, Becky, Margaret, and others, while the authorized opening sustains the same mode. Ryan’s whole-book craft account resolves the structure explicitly, and the NPR review independently corroborates it. Inclusive “we” in q10673 and the first-person material in q10677, q10698, q10702, and q10726 are gnomic commentary, dialogue, or unresolved clipping rather than autonomous first-person base sections. Some individual quotes remain too short to diagnose locally, but no credible evidence suggests sustained first- or second-person narration.
